question: Pipe A can fill a tank alone in 6 hours, Pipe B can fill it in 9 hours, and Pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are initially opened and after 1.5 hours, pipe C is discovered to be leaking and immediately closed, and if the work done by pipe C during the initial 1.5 hours is (x)/(7) \% of the work done by all the three pipes in the initial 1.5 hours, then the number of factors of x is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take LCM = 36 units

Efficiencies: A = 6, B = 4, C = −3

Total = 7 units/hr

C’s share = 3/7 ⇒ % = 300/7 ⇒ x = 300

**∴ Factors of 300 = 18**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A = 6 h, B = 9 h, C = 12 h (emptying)

**Formula used:**

Work = Rate × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B and C = 6 + 4 − 3 = 7 units/hr

⇒ Work done by all in 1.5 h = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 units

⇒ Work done by C = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 units (removed)

⇒ Ratio = 4.5 / 10.5 = 3/7

⇒ Percentage = (3/7) × 100 = 300/7

⇒ x = 300

⇒ 300 = 2² × 3 × 5²

⇒ Number of factors = (2+1)(1+1)(2+1) = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Take LCM as total work to simplify calculations

Outlet Concept

Outlet reduces work, so efficiency is negative

Factors Formula

If n = paqbrc, factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1)
